BEFORE THE GEORGIA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION

Georgia Power Company

STF-DEA Data Request Set No. 8 

BASIS FOR THE ASSERTION THAT THE 
INFORMATION SUBMITTED IS A TRADE SECRET


	As part of Georgia Power Company’s Georgia Power Company’s 2025 Integrated Resource Plan Georgia Power’s Company’s Application for the Certification, Decertification, and Amended Demand Side Management Plan filed in Docket No. 56002, Georgia Power Company (“Georgia Power” or the “Company”) submits to the Georgia Public Service Commission its response to STF-DEA-8-13 (“Response”). In the Response, the Company has provided specific customer information (the “Information”). All such Information constitutes trade secret information of the Southern Company, Georgia Power, and its affiliates and is therefore protected from public disclosure under Commission Rule 515-3-1-.11.

	The Information derives economic value from not being generally known to and not being readily ascertainable by proper means by other persons who can obtain economic value from its disclosure or use. Specifically, the Information contains includes nonpublic, project- and customer-specific cost for transmission projects. Public disclosure could provide contractors, suppliers, and other market participants insight into the Company’s historical transmission project costs. Such parties could use this Information to undermine the Company’s market position and impair the Company’s ability to obtain competitive pricing and manage projects economically for customers. Competitors are not required to disclose similar customer information and to require Georgia Power to do so would put it at an economic disadvantage.

	The Information is subject to substantial procedures to maintain its secrecy. Only select Georgia Power and Southern Company Services personnel are granted access to the Information. Those personnel receive access only on a “need to know” basis. Parties outside the Company who have been granted access to the Information, if any, have been required to sign confidentiality agreements with respect to the Information.

=== DKT 56002 & 56003 STF-DEA-8 PD/STF-DEA-8-16.docx ===
STF-DEA-8-16

Question: 

Georgia Power's TYP project listings reference zone numbers in addition to TEAMS numbers (e.g., in project location or planning area designations.
Please describe the zone numbering methodology, including how zone boundaries are determined, how zone numbers are assigned to projects, and whether zone numbers or boundaries have changed between the 2022 TYP and 2025 TYP.
Please provide a supporting map showing all current transmission planning zones, their boundaries, and zone numbers.

Response: 

The transmission planning zone numbers referenced in the Georgia Ten-Year Transmission Plans (“TYPs”) have remained unchanged for more than a decade. Historically, these planning zones were established to align with what are now legacy service territories that corresponded to Transmission Maintenance Center and Operating Headquarters geographic areas. The boundaries were developed based on the geographic distribution of transmission assets and the operational service areas in place at that time.

For planning and reporting purposes, transmission projects are assigned to a zone based on the location of the associated transmission facilities and their proximity to the applicable legacy service area. The zone designation serves as a geographic reference within the Company's transmission planning documentation.

The transmission planning zone numbering methodology, zone assignments, and zone boundaries did not change between the 2022 TYP and the 2025 TYP. Accordingly, projects identified in the 2022 TYP and 2025 TYP are categorized using the same planning zone framework seen in the STF-DEA-8-16 Attachment.

STF-DEA-8-12

Question: 

If a project scope changes in any way, will the TEAMS number be maintained? What would cause a project’s TEAMS number to change?

Response:

As explained in response to STF-DEA-8-11, TEAMS identifier numbers are not reused or reassigned to different projects. Each TEAMS identifier is a unique project identifier. Project scope may evolve as planning studies progress and system needs change. Depending on the nature and extent of a scope change, the existing TEAMS identifier may remain associated with the project, or a new TEAMS identifier may be created to reflect a materially different project scope. TEAMS identifiers are tracked within the Company’s project management processes.

                             What Has Changed in 2026?

Intent of ANOPR remains the same
 • Standardize and expedite the interconnection of large loads


Key ideas of the ANOPR
 • Access and speed: Equal treatment with steps for faster interconnection
 • Cost control: Large loads pay their fair share
 • Reliability: Keep the grid strong as demand grows


What is next for FERC on this ANOPR?
 • June 18th open meeting should provide additional clarity

                            Georgia Already Doing It Right

Georgia PSC already uses smart rules for large loads
 • Cost Responsibility: Large loads pay for grid upgrades
 • Contract Oversight: PSC reviews large load contracts to protect customers
 • Long-Term Outlook: Integrated long-term planning keeps the grid strong and reliable


Bottom line:
 • State regulated + vertically integrated = Success
 • Georgia’s approach = Affordable, fair, reliable, and ready for continuous growth
